name: Masikoro Malagasy
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: No grammar/phonology of Masikoro; refs are a proverb collection (Raharinjanahary & Velonandro 1995), dialectometry, and ethnography; Vezo/Sakalava works cover other dialects.

new_statements.quote: L'accent tombe le plus souvent sur la pénultième et, dans les mots finissant par -ke ou -tse ou les suffixes -ko ou -ne, sur l'anté-pénultième. [footnote 1, same page:] Le vezo a une tendance à unifier les finales -ke et -tse et même les nasales finales de l'ANC. en -ke. Le sakalava y a emprunté quelques mots dans cette forme.
new_statements.translation: Stress falls most often on the penultimate syllable and, in words ending in -ke or -tse or in the suffixes -ko or -ne, on the antepenultimate. [fn. 1:] Vezo tends to merge the finals -ke and -tse, and even the final nasals of Common Austronesian, into -ke. Sakalava has borrowed a few words in that form.
new_statements.citation: Dahl, Otto Chr. 1968. Contes malgaches en dialecte sakalava: textes, traduction, grammaire et lexique. Oslo: Universitetsforlaget (Instituttet for Sammenlignende Kulturforskning, Ser. B, Skrifter 54). viii+122 pp.
new_statements.locator: p. 4 (grammar sketch, phonology; running footer '4 Contes sakalava'; nb.no scan page 0014). Related: footnote 1 on p. 4 (Vezo finals) and p. 7 (possessive formation: 'mots finissant en -ke ou -tse mais accentués sur la pénultième').
new_statements.rule_in_words: Default penultimate stress; words whose final syllable is one of the weak finals -ke / -tse (the western reflexes of Merina -ka / -tra) or the suffixes -ko / -ne are stressed on the antepenult, i.e. the weak final syllable does not count. This is the standard Malagasy pattern; Dahl states it for the Sakalava of Morondava, the variety Glottolog maps to msh.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any snippet window; the nb.no fragment probe for 'accent secondaire' in the book returned no hit.
new_statements.exceptions: 'Le plus souvent' (most often) penult; antepenult with finals -ke/-tse and suffixes -ko/-ne; p. 7 notes words in -ke/-tse that are nevertheless stressed on the penult ('mots finissant en -ke ou -tse mais accentués sur la pénultième'), i.e. some -ke/-tse words keep penultimate stress. Sentence continues 'Dans ces cas il n'est...' (window cut).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (phonology section of a grammar sketch accompanying narrative texts). Quote is reconstructed from four overlapping verbatim Google Books snippet windows of the same page (each saved), the opening 'L'accent' confirmed by the capitalised hit on nb.no scan page 0014; the full page could not be opened (book in copyright; nb.no copy viewable only from Norway; HathiTrust search-only).
new_statements.identity_note: The deciding statement is from Dahl 1968, a grammar sketch + texts of the 'dialecte sakalava' of Morondava (tales written by Pastor T. Tsiazonaly of Morondava; Ottino's 1971 review places the material on the west coast between Maintirano and the Onilahy, with vocabulary covering Sakalava, Masikoro and Vezo). Glottolog files this work under masi1268 with the language note 'Sakalava of Morondava = Masikoro [msh]'; strictly Morondava is Menabe Sakalava, which a different mapping could put under West Malagasy Sakalava [saka1291/skg]. Dahl's footnote on the same page contrasts Vezo (a masi1268 dialect, vezo1235) with the Sakalava he describes. No source describing the Masikoro dialect proper (Toliara/Miary/Bas-Mangoky) with a stress statement was found.

sources.citation: Howe, Penelope. 2017. Tonogenesis in Central dialects of Malagasy. PhD diss., Rice University.
sources.note: §2.3.6 p. 48: pan-Malagasy penultimate stress; antepenultimate in words with weak finals '-ke, -tse in western and southwestern dialects (Dahl 1952)'. Second-hand on Vezo: 'Poirot 1998: 52 states that stress is strongly marked by duration, with stressed vowels up to a factor of ten longer than unstressed vowels... denies that there is a consistent role of pitch'. No Masikoro-specific location statement.
